classification_rationale: The applicability trigger (an exact-equality `==` comparison against a balance expression -- `address(this).balance == x`, matching the sibling S requirement req-1-exact-balance-check's own wording) is a narrow, well-defined SYNTACTIC pattern: an `==`/`!=` BinaryOperation node where one operand resolves to a `.balance` access. This is genuinely mechanical -- Slither's IR exposes `.balance` member accesses directly, so a custom predicate is plausible (not yet built in this pass; see components below). The CONFORMANCE condition once triggered -- 'MUST protect itself against transfers affecting the balance tested' -- is open-ended: there is no closed list of acceptable protection mechanisms named in the text (could be CEI ordering, a reentrancy guard, snapshotting balance before AND after within the same atomic operation, restricting who can trigger transfers in between, etc.), so evaluating whether a SPECIFIC piece of code's protection is adequate requires semantic judgment, not a second syntactic pattern match.

components.note: Would detect `==`/`!=` comparisons where an operand is a `.balance` access. Scope corrected per AR-002 (rtf/l9_assumptions_register/REGISTER.jsonl): an earlier draft of this component also included ERC20-style `balanceOf()` calls, which is not supported by this requirement's own text ('the balance of an account' names native ETH balance directly, matching req-1-exact-balance-check's wording) -- that was importing an external token-standard convention, caught during a self-review pass before any evaluation ran. Not implemented in this Track A pass -- flagged as the concrete next engineering step for this requirement, not silently assumed to exist.

Consumes the trigger component's located exact-balance-check site(s) and the requirement's context bundle (rtf/track_a/context_bundles/req-2-verify-exact-balance-check.json), asks specifically and only whether the code protects against transfers affecting the tested balance between the check and its use -- depends on the L8 shared LLM Judgment Layer, not yet built (see rtf/l8_llm_judgment_layer/).

trigger_precision_note: This trigger is comparatively NARROW and clean -- a fairly rare, specific syntactic shape (exact-equality against a balance expression) with low expected false-positive surface. Contrast with req-2-overflow-underflow's much coarser trigger below -- this variation in trigger precision, even within the same DETERMINISTIC_TRIGGER_SEMANTIC_CONDITION category, is itself a research-relevant finding about how much the extraction quality varies requirement-to-requirement.
aggregation_rule: applicability_state = APPLICABLE iff trigger-exact-balance-eq fires at least once; conformance_state = semantic-review-transfer-protection's decision (PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE/INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE) when applicable, NOT_APPLICABLE otherwise.
